purpose: Prove durable, Order-fenced, release-before-cancel recovery for an inventory-reserved Order created from an exact published Listing offer.
environment_policy: local, demo, or disposable test tenant only
credentials: environment variables only; never command arguments, scenario files, or ledgers
flow: create and publish one governed Listing offer
place Order from the exact published Listing offer
reserve 2 units and bind the exact reservation to the Order item
submit exactly one durable cancellation Saga START command
let the Saga establish CANCELLATION_PENDING before releasing Inventory
poll the read-only Saga route until COMPLETED or fail closed on MANUAL_REVIEW/timeout
prove the Saga-owned RELEASE is an immutable duplicate and Inventory is 10/0/10/v3
prove the Saga-owned FINALIZE_CANCELLATION is an immutable duplicate and Order is CANCELLED/v4
prove the terminal Order has no payment, fulfillment, or shipment reference
replay all 11 client-issued commands and require immutable duplicate results, including START
invariants: PLACE_FROM_LISTING includes the exact listing_id and listing_offer_id
Saga START contains no fault-injection field
Order enters CANCELLATION_PENDING before any Inventory release, fencing concurrent payment
Saga snapshots the exact TRADE_ORDER reservation, Order ID, Order item ID, SKU, quantity, owner, and warehouse dimension
Saga reaches COMPLETED only after released_reservation_count equals expected_reservation_count
the Saga-owned Inventory RELEASE uses one stable idempotency key and replays as duplicate
the Saga-owned FINALIZE_CANCELLATION uses one stable idempotency key and replays as duplicate
terminal Inventory is exactly on_hand=10, reserved=0, available=10
terminal Order payment_id, fulfillment_id, and shipment_id are all null
the executed-domain ledger contains no payment or fulfillment command
the same START payload returns its immutable initial REQUESTED result as duplicate

failure_policy.retryable: the backend persists RETRY_SCHEDULED with lease and backoff evidence
failure_policy.terminal: MANUAL_REVIEW makes the runner fail closed with only the error code
failure_policy.timeout: the runner fails without issuing RELEASE, CANCEL, RETRY, or fault-injection commands

fault_injection: not exposed by this runner; deterministic recovery faults belong only to backend test scope
cleanup: the release and cancellation are the compensation; retain immutable operation, Saga, history, Outbox, and redacted runner evidence
